task.instructions:
Using matplotlib, read commute.csv (columns: state, minutes) and draw a horizontal Cleveland dot plot of the average commute time for each of the 40 states.
Requirements:
- One circular dot per state, sorted so the state with the LONGEST commute is at the TOP and the shortest at the bottom.
- Show every state name as a y tick label (all 40 must be visible).
- Draw a vertical red dashed line at the median of the 40 values.
- Set the x axis limits to 0..45 and label the x axis 'Average commute (minutes)'.
- Set the title to exactly 'Average commute by state'.
- Make the figure 8 by 11 inches.
- Save the figure at 100 dpi.
Save the figure as figure.png.

function.arguments:
{"command": "cat <<'EOF' > plot_commute.py
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Read the CSV file
commute_data = pd.read_csv('commute.csv')

# Sort by minutes in descending order (longest commute at the top)
sorted_data = commute_data.sort_values(by='minutes', ascending=False)

# Calculate the median
median_commute = sorted_data['minutes'].median()

# Create the figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 11))

# Plot the Cleveland dot plot
for i, row in sorted_data.iterrows():
    ax.scatter(row['minutes'], i, color='blue', s=100, edgecolor='black')

# Add a vertical red dashed line at the median
ax.axvline(x=median_commute, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=1)

# Set x-axis limits and label
ax.set_xlim(0, 45)
ax.set_xlabel('Average commute (minutes)')

# Set y-tick labels to state names
ax.set_yticks(range(len(sorted_data)))
ax.set_yticklabels(sorted_data['state'])

# Set the title
ax.set_title('Average commute by state')

# Remove y-axis label (not needed)
ax.set_ylabel('')

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('figure.png', dpi=100, bbox_inches='tight')

# Show the plot (optional, for verification)
plt.show()
EOF"}
